BEFORE  HON'BLE SHRI JUSTICE G. S. AHLUWALIA  ON THE 7 th OF NOVEMBER, 2025  SECOND APPEAL No. 882 of 2006  SMT. SHANTI DEVI (DEAD) THR. LRS  Versus  RANCHARAN AND OTHERS  Appearance:
 Shri Akshat Kumar Jain - Advocate appellant.
 Shri Yogesh Chaturvedi - Advocate for respondents No.
 ORDER 1.

This Second Appeal under Section 100 of CPC has been filed against the judgment and decree dated 20.09.2006 passed by Fourth Additional District Judge (Fast Track) Shivpuri in Civil Appeal No.121- A/2005, as well as the judgment and decree dated 30.06.2005 passed by Second Civil Judge, Class 2, Shivpuri in Civil Suit No.3A/2005, by which the suit filed by the plaintiff/appellant was dismissed.

sentences.text: 2. The appellant is the plaintiff who has lost her case from both the Courts below.
3. It is not out of place to mention here that initially the suit was dismissed.
The appeal filed by appellant was allowed and matter was remanded back.
The appellate Court had allowed the application filed by appellant under Order 6 Rule 17 CPC and permitted the appellant to amend his plaint.

Accordingly, after remand the plaint was amended to the effect NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:29028 2 SA-882-2006 that plaintiff has been dispossessed during the pendency of suit.

4. The facts necessary for disposal of the present appeal, in short, are that the appellant filed a suit for declaration of title and permanent injunction, pleading inter alia that the plaintiff is the owner and in possession of survey No.652.
The husband of the plaintiff was in possession of 1 bigha and 5 biswa of land, and after his death, the plaintiff is in legal possession of the land in dispute.

Since the plaintiff is of an advanced age, therefore, she is unable to attend the proceedings of the Court,

sentences.text: therefore, her grandson, Anil Sharma, has been appointed as power of attorney holder, and accordingly, the suit was filed through the power of attorney holder.
It is the case of the plaintiff that the total area of survey No.652, was 25 biswa.

The batankan of the said survey took place and survey No.652/2, area 8 biswa; survey No.652/3, area 6 biswa; survey No.652/4, area 8 biswa; and survey No.652/5, area 3 biswa, total 25 biswa, which comes to 1 bigha and 5 biswa were merged and survey No.652, area 1 bigha 5 biswa came into existence.
The plaintiff was in possession of the said land.

5. During the bandobast settlement proceedings, survey No.652 was bifurcated into two survey Nos.,
i.e., 654 and 655.
Survey Nos.654/12 and 655/2 were in the name of the husband of the plaintiff.
Similarly, survey No.654, area 1 bigha and 8 biswa, was recorded in the name of few members of the Scheduled Tribe.
The settlement took place in the year 1972-1973, and new survey numbers were created in place of survey numbers 652, 654, and 655.
At that time, in place of 25 biswa of land, only 16 biswa of land was recorded in the name of plaintiff, and thereafter, in the present scenario,
NEUTRAL
CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:29028 3 SA-882-2006 the total area has been reduced to 12 biswa, whereas there was no reason for the defendant No.3 to reduce the land by 13 biswa.
6. It was pleaded that defendant No.3 has not acquired 13 bigha of land, and defendant No.3 has manipulated the area and the spot map.
Initially, the survey No.652 was of 25 biswa of land.

Thereafter, the survey number was changed to 477, and the area was reduced to 16 biswa, and now,
as per the new survey number 302, the total area has been further reduced to 12 biswa, whereas the defendant No.3 has increased the 3 bigha of land which was standing in the name of defendants No.1 to 2 from 3 bigha and 12 biswa to 5 bigha and 10 biswa, and accordingly, 1 bigha of land was illegally added in the account of defendants No.1 and 2.
However, the plaintiff is still in possession of the land in dispute.

The plaintiff came to know about the manipulation in the year 1993, and accordingly, she filed an application before the revenue court for correction, but since the defendants were belonging to the Scheduled Tribe, therefore, they managed the things and the Revenue Officers did not correct the mistake.
Whereas the plaintiff is still in possession of the property in dispute for the last 40 years.

The defendants are out and out to alienate the property,
and in case 1 bigha and 6 biswa of land belonging to the plaintiff is alienated, then she would suffer irreparable loss.

Accordingly, it was prayed that a declaratory decree be issued to the effect that the plaintiff is entitled to get 25 biswa of land, and by reducing 1 bigha and 8 biswa from survey Nos.
288 and 300, the aforesaid land be given to the plaintiff.

7. After remand by appellate Court, the plaint was amended and it was NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:29028 4 SA-882-2006 claimed that the defendants have taken possession of land in dispute.
However, no prayer for grant of decree for possession was made.
8. The defendant No.1 filed his reply and denied the plaint averments.
The factum of execution of power of attorney was also denied.
It was denied that any manipulation was done in revenue records and it was also denied that any area of survey number has been increased or decreased.
It was denied that any land of the plaintiff was included in the land recorded in the names of defendants No.1 & 2.
Thus, it was denied that the land of the plaintiff has been included in survey Nos.288 and 300.

It was denied that the defendants have taken possession of the land in dispute during the Smt. Shanti Devi vs Rancharan on 7 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/42045746/
2 pendency of the suit.
9.
Defendant No.2 also filed his written statement and denied the plaint averments.
It was claimed that the defendant No.2 was always in possession of survey No.288 and the plaintiff was never dispossessed during the pendency of the suit.
It was also claimed that the suit is barred by time.
10. The trial Court after framing issues and recording evidence dismissed the suit.
11. Being aggrieved by the judgment and decree passed by the Trial Court, the appellant preferred an appeal which too has been dismissed by the Appellate Court.
12. It is submitted by counsel for appellant that the Courts below have wrongly held that plaintiff has failed to prove that land was ever reduced from her land account.
It is also submitted that the Courts below have wrongly held that the suit is barred under Section 257 of MPLR Code.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:29028 5 SA-882-2006

However, it was fairly conceded that in spite of amendment in the plaint to the effect that during pendency of the suit the plaintiff was dispossessed, still no decree for possession was claimed and proposed the following substantial questions of law :
"(1) Whether suit for possession and declaration of title may be filed after arising of cause of action?
(2) Whether possession and title of land may go accordingly?
(3) Whether section 89 of M.P.Land Revenue Code barred the jurisdiction of civil court ?
(4) Whether section 257G of M.P.Land Revenue Code barred the jurisdiction of civil court to decide title and while giving injunction on the basis of title and possession?
(5) Whether the evidence from revenue entries are rebutable and any person can get title from wrong entries however long and possession land may be discarded while deciding the title ?"

13. Heard learned counsel for the parties.
14. Section 257 of MPLR Code reads as under :
"257. Exclusive jurisdiction of revenue authorities.--

Except as otherwise provided in this Code, or in any other enactment for the time being in force, no Civil Court shall entertain any suit instituted or application made to obtain a decision or order on any matter which the State Government, the Board, or any Revenue Officer is by this Code, empowered to determine, decide or dispose of, and in particular and without prejudice to the generality of this provision, no Civil Court shall exercise jurisdiction over any of the following matters : --

sentences.text:
15. Thus, it is clear that where a Revenue Officer is empowered to determine, decide or dispose of,
any question covered under the provisions of Section 257 of MPLR Code, then the jurisdiction of the Civil Court will be barred.
16. It is the case of the appellant that while the settlement proceedings, the area was reduced, and it was merged in Survey Nos.288 and 300.

Section 107 to 110, 113 to 115 of the MPLR Code deals with various NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:29028 8 SA-882-2006 provisions including maps of villages showing the boundaries of the survey numbers and block numbers, record of rights, correction of errors,
correction of wrong or incorrect entry in land record, mutation of acquisition of right in land records, etc.
All these powers are to be exercised exclusively by the revenue authorities.
17. Furthermore, Lakshminarayan (PW-2) who is the son of the plaintiff and father of the power of attorney holder, has admitted that he had filed an appeal against the settlement proceedings.

Furthermore, in paragraph 11 of his cross-examination, he has further stated that when he purchased the land, then he found that a part of his land has been merged in Survey No.300, and he has further stated that he had purchased the land about two years prior to the recording of his evidence.
Smt. Shanti Devi vs Rancharan on 7 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/42045746/
5 18.

Furthermore, after the matter was remanded back again a fresh affidavit under Order 18 Rule 4 CPC, on behalf of Lakshminarayan was filed, and he was further cross-examined, and in that cross-examination also he admitted that he had moved the revenue Courts for correction of revenue records, but what transpired in those proceedings has not been placed on record by the plaintiff.
19.

Under these circumstances, this Court is of considered opinion that since the basic case of the plaintiff was only to the effect that the land which was originally the part of Survey No.652 was partially merged in Survey Nos.288 and 300 during the bandobast proceedings, then the dispute raised by the plaintiff was exclusively triable by the revenue Court.
No question of title was involved.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:29028 9 SA-882-2006 20.

Under these circumstances, the Courts below did not commit any error in holding that the suit filed by the appellant was barred by the provisions of Section 257 of MPLR Code.
21.

Furthermore, it appears that after the civil suit was dismissed by the trial Court by its judgment dated 29/1/2003, the appellant preferred Civil Appeal No.9A/2003 and in that appeal, an application under Order 6 Rule 17 CPC was filed by the plaintiff, thereby seeking permission to amend the plaint to the effect that the plaintiff was dispossessed during the pendency of the suit.
The said application was allowed, and the matter was remanded back.

22. The amendment which was carried out by the plaintiff in the plaint, reads as under:
"5

If this amendment is read, then it is clear that the plaintiff had claimed that during the pendency of suit, she was dispossessed, but by making an attempt to cleverly draft the amendment, it was claimed by the plaintiff that in view of the provisions of Section 52 of Transfer of Property Act (lis pendens), the plaintiff is still in legal possession of the land in dispute.
24.

Accordingly, the counsel for the appellant was directed to explain that how the principle of lis pendens would apply to the facts of the case, NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:29028 10 SA-882-2006 specifically when there is no allegation of alienation.

It was fairly conceded by counsel for the appellant that if the plaintiff was dispossessed during the pendency of suit, then the principle of lis pendens would not apply, as there was no sale deed, as it is the case of the plaintiff that her land has been included in the revenue records in the land of Ramcharan/defendant No.1.
25.
Thus, it is clear that according to the plaintiff, she was dispossessed during the pendency of suit.

Under these circumstances, it was incumbent upon the plaintiff to seek a decree for possession,
which was not done.

sentences.text: It is well-established principle of law that this Court, in exercise of power under Section 100 of CPC, can interfere with the concurrent findings of facts, only when they are found to be perverse.

This Court cannot substitute its finding of fact even if the concurrent facts are found to be erroneous.
27.
As no perversity could be pointed out by the counsel for the appellant, accordingly this Court is of considered opinion that no substantial question of law arises in the present appeal.
28. Accordingly, the appeal fails and is hereby dismissed.

(G. S. AHLUWALIA) JUDGE Aman Smt. Shanti Devi vs Rancharan on 7 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/42045746/
